Based on the aforementioned analysis of the peer-reviewed articles, the authors propose a novel multidimensional taxonomy categorized through three lenses - coordination mechanisms, algorithmic nature, and collective behaviours - aiming to provide a structured overview of the swarming paradigms in the literature.
tags: electrical engineering, electronic engineering, information engineering

name: Lorenz Airspace Protocol Proposal: Market-Based Low-Altitude Airspace Coordination for eVTOL Operations
abstract: This paper introduces the Lorenz Airspace Protocol (LAPP), a coordination framework for dense low-altitude electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) traffic operating between 1,000 and 1,800 feet above ground level. LAPP combines a heading-based altitude stratification scheme (the hemispheric rule, extended to eight directional sectors) with a market-based slot allocation mechanism using sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auctions at route turn points. The protocol reserves capacity for emergency and public-safety operations at zero cost, funded by commercial auction revenues. We present results from an agent-based reference simulator demonstrating that: (1) a lane tolerance of 5-7° minimizes conflicts under uniform traffic assumptions; (2) stricter tolerances beyond this optimum increase conflicts due to turn-point clustering, producing a characteristic U-shaped tradeoff curve; (3) auction-based allocation achieves superior allocative efficiency compared to first-come-first-served (FCFS), directing scarce slots to highest-priority traffic; and (4) layer transition dynamics introduce a new category of vertical conflict whose precise characterization requires higher-fidelity simulation than the present reference implementation provides. LAPP is proposed as an open protocol standard for interoperable eVTOL airspace coordination, with a revenue model that funds infrastructure through market-priced slot allocation.
tags: electrical engineering, electronic engineering, information engineering

name: 2025 International Conference on Low-Altitude Airspace and Artificial Intelligence (LAAI)
Application of Reinforcement Learning in Low-Altitude Edge Computing Resource Allocation
abstract: In order to solve the problem that traditional allocation strategies are difficult to meet the real-time and efficiency due to the strong dynamics of resources and uncertain task requirements in low-altitude edge computing environment, this paper proposes a resource allocation framework driven by deep reinforcement learning. By constructing a multi-dimensional state space that integrates UAV position, edge node load, communication state and task priority, a weighted reward function that considers both response delay and resource utilization is designed, and an action smoothness constraint and priority experience replay mechanism are introduced to improve the stability of the strategy and the adaptability to burst traffic. Furthermore, transfer learning and federated learning are combined to enhance the cross-scenario generalization and privacy protection ability of the algorithm. The experiment is based on a high-fidelity simulation environment with a density of 300 users /km2and a flight speed of 30 m/s. The results show that compared with the traditional heuristic and mainstream reinforcement learning algorithms, the average response delay of the proposed method is reduced by 19.7%, the resource utilization rate is increased by 25%, the task completion rate is increased by 14.3%, and the convergence speed is increased by 37.6%. The success rate of policy transfer reaches 89.4%. The study confirms the superiority and robustness of deep reinforcement learning in resource management of complex low-altitude environment, which provides a feasible technical path and theoretical support for future intelligent low-altitude system.

General Aviation: A Mature Economy in Low-Altitude Airspace
IEEE Standard for a Framework for Structuring Low-Altitude Airspace for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Operations
abstract: A structure of low-altitude airspace for efficient unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) traffic management is defined in this standard. The standard elaborates the structural low altitude based on UAV low-altitude public air routes from five parts: grid technology, remote sensing data, communication and networking, route planning, operation, and management.

name: Table of Contents
Preface :LAAI 2025
abstract: It is with great enthusiasm that we present the proceedings of the 2025 International Conference on Low-Altitude Airspace and Artificial Intelligence (LAAI 2025). As low-altitude airspace emerges as a critical frontier for urban mobility, logistics innovation, and smart city development, the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) has become indispensable to addressing its unique challenges-from dynamic airspace management and real-time traffic optimization to safety assurance and regulatory compliance. LAAI 2025 marks a pivotal platform where researchers, engineers, policymakers, and industry leaders converge to explore how AI can unlock the full potential of low-altitude airspace while ensuring efficiency, security, and sustainability.

name: Organizing Committee :LAAI 2025
Half Title Page
Toward a Safer Low-Altitude Airspace in Urban Environments: Risk and Airspace Availability in Central Wuhan
abstract: This study quantitatively evaluates the potential of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAVs) operations across different urban functional units, providing a fine-grained understanding of how built form, population density, and regulatory constraints affect low-altitude airspace usability. Using voxel-based spatial modeling and visibility analysis, this study assesses available airspace layers and operational feasibility in four urban regions: central core, historical-commercial, industrial, and community zones. The results reveal pronounced spatial heterogeneity. The central core with high building density and population exposure exhibits lower airspace availability, restricting UAV applications mainly to emergency and inspection tasks. Historical-commercial zones face similar constraints due to heritage protection and narrow streets, although peripheral areas have moderate availability and are suitable for controlled operations, such as façade inspection and fire monitoring. In contrast, industrial areas exhibit the highest operational potential, providing natural UAV corridors ideal for logistics and factory inspections. Residential communities have intermediate availability, necessitating context-sensitive governance to balance service convenience with social tolerance.By integrating spatial simulation results with functional differentiation, this research proposes a conceptual framework for parcel-level airspace governance that emphasizes different vertical zones analogous to land-use regulations. The findings highlight the need for safety–efficiency trade-offs tailored to urban functions, informing planning policy and operational guidelines for future low-altitude urban management. This study contributes to the emerging discourse on three-dimensional urban governance by providing a quantitative foundation for the adaptive, safe, and efficient integration of UAVs into complex city environments.

name: Design of Airport Low-Altitude Traffic Control System Architecture Based on Cloud-Edge Collaboration and Deep Learning
abstract: This study addresses the real-time and intelligent needs of low-altitude airspace traffic management in airports by designing a system architecture based on cloud-edge collaboration and deep learning. Analyzing the high latency and resource bottleneck issues of traditional centralized cloud architectures, we propose an edge computing layer using Huawei Atlas 500 nodes and the KubeEdge platform, combined with federated learning to optimize the flight path model in the cloud, achieving efficient data processing and model updates. The system utilizes OpenEuler and GaussDB for domestic software compatibility, and achieves Level 3 security certification, ensuring compliance and security in a domestically-developed environment. Experimental results show that this architecture reduces latency from 50ms to 8ms, improves model accuracy to 95%, and achieves 85% resource utilization, significantly enhancing the performance and reliability of lowaltitude traffic management. This provides a feasible solution for intelligent air traffic management.
tags: electrical engineering, electronic engineering, information engineering

name: Safely enabling UAS operations in low-altitude airspace
abstract: NASA is developing a system to safely enable low altitude unmanned aerial system (UAS) operations. The system is referred to as UAS Traffic Management (UTM). The UTM will safely enable a variety of business models and multiple operations in the same airspace. The UTM will provide services such as airspace configuration and geo-fencing, weather and wind integration, demand-capacity imbalance management, and separation management, and contingency management. The UTM research and development has been conducted in collaboration with many in industry, academia, and government. The UTM system will evolve through four builds. Each build will be collaboratively tested with partners. The final prototype will be available for persistent daily use of UAS operations beyond line of sight.

name: Addressing the low-altitude airspace integration challenge: USS or UTM core?
abstract: Provides an abstract of the keynote presentation and may include a brief professional biography of the presenter. The complete presentation was not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

name: Research, Analysis and Improvement of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Path Planning Algorithms in Urban Ultra-Low Altitude Airspace
abstract: Urban ultra-low altitude airspace (ULAA) presents unique challenges for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) path planning due to high building density and regulatory constraints. This study analyzes and improves classical path planning algorithms for UAVs in ULAA. Experiments were conducted using A*, RRT, RRT*, and artificial potential field (APF) methods in a simulated environment based on building data from Chengdu City, China. Results show that traditional algorithms struggle in dense obstacle environments, particularly APF due to local minima issues. Enhancements were proposed: a density-aware heuristic for A*, random perturbation for APF, and a hybrid optimization strategy for RRT*. These modifications improved computation time, path length, and obstacle avoidance. The study provides insights into the limitations of classical algorithms and suggests enhancements for more effective UAV path planning in urban environments.
tags: electrical engineering, electronic engineering, information engineering

name: Cargo Drone Airspace Integration in Very Low Level Altitude
abstract: Current initiatives to integrate UAS into airspace mostly target small or medium-sized drones. However, it is foreseeable that there will be a demand for cargo UAS with a payload in the range of about 1000 kg. It is proving to be a challenge to integrate these larger drones into a national airspace. The concept of choice for this problem is to use the EASA Specific Category. In this category it is possible that the reliability of the vehicles is not maximised by increasingly complex system components, but that the drones are guided on special trajectories so that any accident that occurs does not result in fatalities and only financial losses. The advantage is that the concept can be realized with existing technology and only moderate effort for new equipment on board and on ground. However, this poses some further challenges to air traffic procedures. In Germany and Europe in general, the airspace is densely occupied, especially near airports. UAS missions should disturb this existing structure as little as possible. An integration concept must therefore ensure that the future air cargo system can strategically or at least tactically avoid any potential risk, regardless of whether it is a conurbation, an industrial infrastructure or other aircraft. We present an integration concept for airspace structure, communication infrastructure and information management. Based on publicly available data on population and ground infrastructure, we present exemplary calculations that show the concept’s feasibility.

name: A Digital Twin-Driven Computation and Analysis Framework for Low-Altitude Airspace
abstract: Abstract To address key challenges in low-altitude airspace management, such as high dynamic complexity, significant safety risks, and information fragmentation, a digital twin-based methodology for low-altitude airspace computation and analysis is proposed in this paper. First, a four-layer digital twin system architecture is established. High-fidelity digital twin mapping of the low-altitude airspace is achieved through the integration of multi-source heterogeneous data, the application of unified spatio-temporal representation, the implementation of dynamic evolution modeling, and the facilitation of bidirectional physical-virtual closed-loop interaction. Second, innovative intelligent algorithms, including a bidirectional GRU-Seq2Seq trajectory prediction model and a Kalman filter-based error compensation mechanism, are incorporated. These components form a comprehensive technical framework that supports quantitative airspace resource evaluation, real-time trajectory analysis, and conflict prediction and early warning. Finally, experimental validation is conducted across three scenarios: single-target conventional flight, multi-target collaborative flight, and extreme weather interference. The results indicate that, compared with the conventional geometric twin approach, the proposed method achieves a 37.2% reduction in trajectory deviation, a 62.5% improvement in conflict warning accuracy, and a 28.6% enhancement in site selection safety. Furthermore, it is shown to outperform traditional methods across five core performance metrics, including computational efficiency and trajectory accuracy, which further confirms its strong suitability for supporting the high-quality development of the low-altitude economy.
tags: electrical engineering, electronic engineering, information engineering

name: A Spatially Structured Collision Avoidance Model for Low-Altitude Uav Navigation in Multi-Layered Airspace
Alternate Traffic Path Optimization Algorithm by Multi Metrics
abstract: This technical paper describes two factors involved in selection and optimization of alternate routes for its working route. The first is from the point of view of topology survivability to make the alternate routes generated are node-dis-jointed to each other, and are all nodes dis-jointed to their working route. The feature of node dis-joint of alternate routes helps to get better availability of communication path to improve the reliability of traffic transferring when working route gets into malfunction. Another is the reliability evaluation of alternate routes, which considers the reliability of all nodes and links along the route. Evaluating alternate route's reliability is necessary to optimize them to acquire the best alternate route for standby. Based on the two factors above, two metrics are defined in the paper, one is Maximum Node-Disjoint Path (MNDP) which is used to compute most available alternate routes which are node dis-jointed, and another is Most Reliable Replacement Node-disjoint Path (MRRNP) which is utilized to optimize alternate routes generated to find the best alternate route by reason of path reliability. Algorithms are put forward to search for node dis-jointed working route and its alternate routes, and to compute reliability of all alternate routes as well as that of their working route. Finally, the paper gives numerical results computed on the example topology of a network, The results demonstrate usage and functions of multiple metrics to decide alternate routes to be taken, and to optimize them further to select the best one of them.

name: An Explainable Safety Assessment and Decision Framework for UAV Emergency Landing in Urban Low-Altitude Airspace
abstract: Emergency landing is a critical safety function for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) operating in urban low-altitude airspace, where complex environments and ground-risk exposure impose stringent requirements on both landing-site selection and approach-trajectory safety. To address this challenge, this paper presents a semantic-driven and explainable safety assessment and decision framework for UAV emergency landing. From scene-level semantic information, the proposed method constructs complementary safety representations that explicitly characterize touchdown-area feasibility, overflight risk distribution, and hard exclusion zones around high-risk entities. Based on fixed feasibility constraints, a diverse set of non-overlapping emergency landing zone (ELZ) candidates is generated to support consistent and reproducible evaluation.To enable end-to-end assessment, a unified safety evaluation protocol is further developed to quantify site-level safety, path-level safety, and their combined global safety. This formulation provides an interpretable decomposition of safety factors and enables direct comparison across different decision strategies. Experimental results in simulation-consistent urban environments demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently improves end-to-end emergency landing safety compared with representative site-only and path-only decision baselines. In particular, the joint decision strategy achieves the best global safety performance with improved robustness, while the heading-aware planner yields higher overflight safety than geometric shortest-path and semantic A* baselines. These results indicate that explicitly coupling landing-site feasibility and trajectory safety is beneficial for reliable emergency landing decision-making. Beyond algorithmic design, this work establishes a standardized and data-driven safety assessment benchmark, providing a principled foundation for future learning-based and safety-critical UAV emergency landing systems.
tags: electrical engineering, electronic engineering, information engineering

name: Characteristics of Jet Stream in Low-altitude Airspace and Impact to Fog in Tianjin Urban Areas
abstract: This study analyzed the temporal and spatial distribution characteristics of jet stream in low airspace (1500 meters) and the impact to fog in Tianjin urban areas, based on the data of the boundary layer wind profiler and the 255 m Meteorological Tower during 2016-2018.The statistical results show that: (1) As for the distribution height of wind jet stream, there are two peak heights within 1500 m, one peak is within 500-600 m, about 23% of the wind stream jet is located at the height; The other peak is located in the 200-300 m range, and about 19% of the jet stream is located at the height; and wind jet streams are more evenly distributed in other low-altitudes airspace. (2) As for the height and frequency seasonal distribution characteristics of the jet stream, the average height of the jet stream is generally located at 700-1000 m, and the seasonal variation of the jet height is not obvious, but the height of the cold season is higher than that of the warm season. The frequency of stream jet in 300-1500 m layer is the lowest in December and the highest in May. In contrast, the low-level jet within the 300 m layer occurs more frequently during the transition from warm to cold season, accounting for about 70% in autumn and winter, with the lowest frequency in June and the highest in October. (3) As for the diurnal distribution characteristics and wind direction of the jet stream, the frequency of wind stream jet at 300-1500 m layer increased at sunset, and the high frequency lasted until dawn of the next day, the character is the same for the low-altitude jet below 300 m, and the frequency during nighttime is more than 70%, far more than the frequency of wind jet at the upper layer. The prevailing jet direction is southwest, accounting for 47%; Followed by northerly wind, accounting for 17%; The southeast (90-180&#176;) jet direction is less than 20%, while the northwest low-level jet stream least frequent. (4) The southerly jet before the fog, which was conducive to the formation of fog, transported water vapor to the fog area; while the northerly jet have bidirectional effect of leading to fog burst or dissipation, which afford to the fog area with cold air and kinetic energy.In conclusion, Due to sparse vertical layer data, such as the FNL reanalysis data, the features of low-altitude airspace jet are rough, especially those below 300 meters. This study supplemented the understanding of the distribution characteristics of the low-altitude jet under 300 m and the effect to fog in Tianjin urban area, which is important for fog forecasting and low-altitude flight meteorological service .&#160;

name: Low Altitude Airspace: A Property Rights No-Man's Land
Hybrid Optimization Algorithm and Transformer Design for Low-Resource Chinese-African Neural Machine Translation
abstract: With the continuous development of China Africa economic and trade relations, the demand for multilingual information transmission on translation tasks is also constantly increasing. Traditional translation methods have shortcomings in efficiency and accuracy, making it difficult to cope with complex economic and trade exchanges. This article proposes an algorithm architecture for intelligent management and optimization of multilingual resources based on a machine translation framework. It carries out cleaning, denoising, matching and other work at the data level to ensure resource quality; Enhance cross linguistic semantic modeling ability through neural network layers and fusion attention mechanisms; Realize self optimization iteration through deep neural networks and hybrid pattern structures. The experiment aimed to verify economic and trade texts, and the results showed a significant improvement in translation accuracy and efficiency. It can effectively solve the problem of multilingual corpus and achieve excellent application effects in practical translation, model stability, and application. It can provide technical and methodological support for cross-border e-commerce, contract translation, and government policy interpretation in China and Africa.

name: Agent-Based Grid Airspace Modeling and Collaborative Decision-Making for Low-Altitude Flight
abstract: To address the growing demand for real-time coordination and distributed management in dynamically evolving low-altitude traffic environments, this study proposes an agent-based grid airspace model together with a MADDPG-based distributed cooperative decision-making (MDCD) framework. The low-altitude airspace is discretized into a three-dimensional grid, where each cell is modeled as an autonomous agent equipped with local state perception and decision-making capabilities. Access permissions and priority weights are dynamically up dated by each grid agent according to local traffic conditions, neighboring cell occupancy, and its own accessibility status. These updated states are then broadcast as local observations to unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) agents. Under a centralized training and distributed execu tion (CTDE) paradigm, cooperative policies are jointly learned by both grid and UAV agents. Simulation results in a three-dimensional grid environment demonstrate that, after sufficient training, the proposed MDCD framework enables all UAVs to successfully reach their desig nated target cells. Moreover, ablation studies reveal that both grid-provided observations and their directional consistency play a crucial role in UAV decision-making. These results validate the effectiveness of incorporating active grid agents into cooperative flight control and pro vide a solid experimental basis for developing distributed low-altitude airspace management strategies.

name: Convective Weather Avoidance Modeling in Low-Altitude Airspace
abstract: Thunderstorms are a leading cause of delay in the National Airspace System (NAS), and significant research has been conducted to predict the areas pilots will avoid during a storm. An example of such research is the Convective Weather Avoidance Model (CWAM), which provides the likelihood of pilot deviation due to convective weather in a given area. This paper extends the scope of CWAM to include low-altitude flights, which typically occur below the tops of convective weather and have slightly different operational constraints. In general, the set of low-altitude flights includes short-hop routes and low-altitude escape routes used to reduce the impact of convective weather in the terminal area. This paper will discuss the classification procedure, present the performance of low-altitude CWAM on observed and forecasted weather, analyze areas of poor performance, and suggest potential improvements to the model. I. Introduction ONVECTIVE weather is a significant impediment to effective and efficient Air Traffic Management (ATM) decisions, and sometimes results in unnecessary delays to the National Airspace System (NAS). In the NAS, 70% of delays are caused by weather, and of those delays, 60% are specifically accounted for by convective weather [1]. Currently, rerouting decisions made by air traffic managers are aided by weather products such as the Corridor Integrated Weather System (CIWS) and the National Convective Weather Forecast (NCWF) [2, 3]. In a Next Generation ATM system, decision support tools such as the Route Availability Planning Tool (RAPT) will mitigate weather-induced delays by supplementing the situational awareness of an air traffic manager with a forecast of the availability of specific flight routes [4]. RAPT is based on the Convective Weather Avoidance Model (CWAM), which is a probabilistic model of pilot decision making in the presence of convective weather [5]. CWAM is a tool originally developed for the en route flight regime to predict pilot deviation decisions by correlating in-flight deviations of aircraft to the weather features they encounter. The model is based on a database comprised of the deviation decision of each flight and weather statistics along each route, which are obtained from CIWS. Pattern classification experiments on the en route CWAM database show that the most descriptive predictors for deviation are related to echo top height, where the most descriptive is the difference in altitude between the aircraft and the echo top height [5]. In the terminal area, deviations are predicted with a different set of features. Several studies of the Dallas and Memphis areas using weather information from the Integrated Terminal Weather System (ITWS) show that deviation decisions are closely related to the radar intensity of the storm and the proximity of the aircraft to the airport [6, 7]. This paper presents the development of a low-altitude version of CWAM which is based on a database composed of weather encounters that occur during level flight between FL100 and FL240. This model is applicable to jet traffic that uses low altitude air routes to „escape‟ from terminal areas when weather or volume congestion impacts lead to constraints on high-altitude airspace, or to low-altitude flight by regional jets on „short hop‟ routes. Such traffic is common in major metroplex airspaces. In this analysis, flight trajectories are obtained from the Enhanced Traffic Management System (ETMS) database, and weather data are acquired from CIWS for 23 convective weather days across two geographical regions (Chicago and New York). A Gaussian classifier is used to determine a set of deviation predictors and the results are tested on observed and forecasted data. The predictor performance is compared to the existing terminal departure CWAM used in RAPT, and the differences are discussed.

name: Application of New ATM Technologies in Low-Altitude Airspace Management
abstract: Management of low-altitude space faces many problems, including safety monitoring, flight information service, operation of ATM (Air Traffic Management) and so on. Because of its opening, new ATM technologies must be taken to solve these problems and thus to improve the safety and efficiency in using the low-altitude space resource. For this purpose, this paper describes in detail the problems of low-altitude space management, analyzes new technologies for solving various problems.

name: Brief Analysis of Main Safety Hazards for Unmanned Aerial System in Low Altitude Airspace
abstract: In low altitude airspace, Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) often face many security threats, which pose enormous challenges to the development of low altitude industries and the construction of low altitude economies.This paper analyzes the main security risk factors from the perspectives of UAVs flight physical failures, low altitude early warning detection network, UAVs communication link defects and information security threats, among which the related threat issues are briefly discussed, such as poor flexibility of UAVs flying on fixed routes, vulnerability to attack during approach reconnaissance, electromagnetic interference emitted by low altitude defense systems and the change of flight control right of Wi-Fi link signals and onboard flight control systems.The results of this paper are helpful for the safety risk assessment of UAVs.

name: Research on the Key Technologies of Low-Altitude Airspace Surveillance and Navigation System
abstract: With the low-altitude airspace opening, the role of surveillance technology in ATC system has increasing prominent. This article used application of image extraction technology, algorithm processing, data fusion and transmission to improve the reliability of surveillance and set up a new structure of network. Finally, we used computers to achieve a new type of low-altitude surveillance system.

name: Low-altitude Airspace UAV Management Based on Intent Driven and Digital Twin System
abstract: With the development of the low-altitude economy, a massive number of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are being deployed in logistics, cruising, communication, and other scenarios, leading to a rapid increase in collision risks. To enhance safety, a structured management method for UAVs in low-altitude airspace is proposed. This method utilizes an intent-driven digital twin system that organizes low-altitude airspace into layers and facilitates the planning of UAV cruising paths. This study simulates the energy consumption and collision risk of logistic, cruising, and communication UAVs in layered airspace under four types of cruising routes, with the collision risk in unstructured airspace simulated as a control group. The approach aims to reduce collision conflicts among UAVs and between UAVs and terrestrial structures, while simultaneously improving UAV performance and energy efficiency. The cruising patterns include various strategies such as random cruising, circular cruising, hovering, vertical boundary cruising, and coordinated cruising with a single UAV. Ultimately, the management of UAV layers and cruising strategies for multiple intent-driven UAVs are integrated and coordinated within the digital twin system, effectively reducing UAV collision risks and energy consumption.
tags: electrical engineering, electronic engineering, information engineering

name: Multi-Source Elastic Fusion Navigation Technology for Low-Altitude Airspace
abstract: Low-altitude airspace refers to the non-regulated airspace below 3000 meters. Compared to the clean airspace, low-altitude airspace has more complex multipath effects, obstruction interference, and other issues. The traditional inertial navigation system (INS) and global satellite navigation system (GNSS) combination will be challenged in terms of positioning accuracy and robustness. The development of 5G positioning technology provides a new solution for the GNSS interference problem in low-altitude areas. The research on multi-source elastic fusion navigation of INS/GNSS/5G positioning was conducted. Based on the state covariance matrix and innovation characteristics during the Kalman filtering process, a multi-source elastic Kalman filter (MsEKF) algorithm based on elastic fusion and optimal information allocation was proposed. This algorithm can effectively isolate local filtering faults and achieve the optimal fusion of multi-sensor information. Finally, taking the low-altitude trajectory as the verification object and setting GNSS and 5G positioning abnormal segments for simulation experiments, the results show that the INS/GNSS/5G positioning combination MsEKF algorithm can effectively solve the GNSS obstruction interference problem, and the RMSE of latitude, longitude and altitude all reach sub-meter level. Compared with the traditional federated Kalman filter (CFKF), the improvement rates are 69.7%, 50.9% and 46.0% respectively.

name: Low-Power ADS-B for GA Operating in Low Altitude Airspace
abstract: Complete and reliable awareness about surrounding traffic is a key pre-requisite of safe operations in any airspace. Performance of such traffic surveillance functions is usually much higher when directly supported by on-board systems of the monitored aircraft, and the term cooperative surveillance is then used for such capability. Nevertheless, operational benefits associated with the latter are directly depending on the amount of fleet equipped with such systems. This paper describes the situation associated with the latest deployment of Automatic Dependent Surveillance - Broadcast (ADS-B) and discusses the possible ways how to extend the ratio of aircraft equipped with such capability in Europe (beyond the current mandate taking effect after June 2020) while mitigating the risk of spectrum congestion, namely considering 1090 MHz frequency.

name: Predictive Analytics of Adolescent Behavioral Patterns for Mental Health Forecasting
abstract: Mental health issues have become a pressing global concern, affecting a growing number of adolescents. Many individuals experience psychological distress without timely recognition, as traditional assessment methods relying heavily on subjective self-reports that often suffer from bias, delayed detection, and underreporting. This gap leads to exacerbated mental health deterioration, impacting quality of life, academic performance, and social functioning, underscoring the urgent need for objective, real-time prediction tools. The study addresses this need by developing a multimodal machine learning framework for early mental state forecasting, with significant implications for enabling proactive interventions and alleviating healthcare burdens. The study utilizes a dataset that integrate diverse mental health factors including demographics, stress triggers, performance metrics (CGPA), satisfaction scores, and lifestyle data. For methodology, the study first preprocesses data through normalization, missing value imputation, and feature extraction to identify behavioral patterns. Then, the study compares four types of machine learning models: logistic regression, support vector machine (SVM), random forest, and XGBoost. Evaluates the model performances based on accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC. Preliminary results show the proposed framework outperforms baseline models, with XGBoost achieving the highest AUC-ROC of 0.9610, demonstrating strong capability in distinguishing mental health states. These findings validate the potential of multimodal data and optimized machine learning algorithms in mental health prediction. Looking forward, the study aims to expand datasets with more diverse populations, refine feature engineering, and enhance real-world applicability, striving to develop a scalable system that improves adolescent mental health monitoring and intervention efficacy.

name: Research on Trajectory Tracking Algorithm for Multi-Joint Arm Coordination
abstract: Aiming at the cooperative trajectory tracking problem of multi-joint arm system, this research proposes an integrated algorithm framework integrating adaptive control, anti-interference communication and energy-saving optimization, aiming at achieving high precision, strong robustness and low energy consumption.

name: Addressing the low-altitude airspace integration challenge — USS or UTM core?
abstract: Advancements in unmanned aerial systems (UAS) technology are invigorating the aviation industry. Integrating these platforms into low-altitude airspace globally is challenging the conventional, safety-first culture of the aviation community. Ideas ranging from segregated airspace to integrating unmanned systems alongside manned aviation within national airspace systems have emerged. This paper will examine the many challenges and approaches to ensure the world's airspace systems can maintain exceptional levels of safety while accommodating and balancing the wave of aviation advancements that will disrupt low-altitude operations in both controlled and uncontrolled airspace. Globally, air navigation service providers (ANSPs) and civil aviation authorities (CAAs) generally agree that new, commercially viable approaches must be developed to promote the use of unmanned systems while ensuring the safety of the existing airspace structure. Safety has always driven advancements in aviation and must continue to do so in the new era of unmanned platforms. UAS Traffic Management (UTM) for low-altitude airspace reinforces this need and provides a path forward for safe integration of all vehicles. The unique nature of the UAS operating environment puts UTM in the position of balancing the safety-critical responsibilities associated with low-altitude airspace management with the commercial obligations connected to interfacing with UAS operators. One model being examined in the United States today is being driven from an operator perspective, or UAS Service Suppliers (USS). The USS function delivers both mission planning for UAS operators as well as serving as distributed airspace managers through some as-yet-defined peer-to-peer coordination process. This is referred to as the operator driven model. With no single USS being the authoritative system, the current concept relies on USS to USS communication and collaboration to share position information and mission planning elements to reduce the risks of conflicts in the airspace. This approach, if widely accepted beyond the research and development phase, could usher in a major shift in airspace integration and management philosophy. Longer-term, this could be a shift from ANSPs being the responsible authority for low-altitude airspace and allocating it to third-party commercial providers. The concept of an operator centric airspace management model is a major technological and philosophical shift from today's aviation industry approach and deserves close examination and consideration. An alternative approach proposed in this paper introduces the concept of a UTM Core platform to alleviate these challenges by allocating the safety-critical, airspace management functions from the collection of USSs to a centralized function. The UTM Core concept will reduce the need for excessive coordination and provide a centralized source for information exchange among all relevant stakeholders. It will address the challenges brought on by inter-USS communication and the collaborative structure the USS centric approach is built upon. As a result, the UTM Core will promote the innovation of new USS entrants by providing the airspace domain expertise required for maintaining the safety of the existing airspace structure. The UTM Core represents an intermediate approach in the progression of an emerging industry. It seeks to build off of the positive progress made towards large-scale UAS integration and introduce new solutions to the challenges it currently faces. This approach retains the possibility of competition for service provision, if desired, and the application of advanced automation to enable a dynamic and economically efficient solution. The UTM Core presents a reasonable path forward that should be considered to maintain the outstanding levels of safety that the aviation community enjoys and expects today.

name: Volumization and Inverse Volumization for Low-Altitude Airspace Geofencing
abstract: View Video Presentation: https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2021-2383.vid The number of Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) operations is expected to increase dramatically with emerging applications in package delivery, search and rescue, recreation, photography, and surveillance. UAS Traffic Management (UTM) has been proposed to safely and efficiently manage low-altitude airspace. Airspace geofencing is a key capability for safe flight. Geofenced airspace volumes can be allocated to safely contain compatible UAS flight operations within a fly-zone (keep-in geofence) and assure avoidance of no-fly zones (keep-out geofences). This paper proposes operational volumization and inverse volumization algorithms to support airspace geofence management for UTM. Layered polygon geofence volumes with constant-altitude floors and ceilings enclose user-input waypoint-based flight plans, and a family of conflict-free flight planning solutions is proposed for inverse volumization. Monte Carlo simulations statistically validate our geofencing algorithms and identify corner cases.

name: Risk-informed UAV operations in urban low-altitude airspace: Implications for transport policy and airspace management
Regional Road Traffic Volume Prediction Based on Deep Learning
abstract: With the increasing complexity of urban road networks, accurate traffic volume prediction has become crucial for intelligent transportation systems (ITS). This study investigates the performance of three deep learning models—Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and Long Short-Term Memory with Attention Mechanism—using the “Metro Interstate Traffic Volume” dataset, which includes hourly traffic data along with weather, holiday and related environmental information. After preprocessing and feature selection, the models were trained to forecast short-term traffic volume based on historical trends and exogenous factors. Evaluation metrics such as R2, MAE, RMSE, and MAPE reveal that the LSTM+Attention model significantly outperforms both baseline LSTM and GRU models. Specifically, the LSTM+Attention achieves the highest R2(0.9814) and the lowest MAPE (9.4860%), demonstrating significantly enhanced prediction accuracy and robustness. These findings confirm that incorporating attention mechanisms effectively improves model performance, offering valuable and important insights for urban traffic forecasting and intelligent decision-making in ITS.

name: Minimum risk low altitude airspace integration for larger cargo UAS
abstract: Current initiatives for UAS airspace integration mostly aim at small or medium sized drones. However, it can be foreseen that there will be a demand of cargo UAS for payload in the range of about 1000 kilograms. It proves to be a challenge to integrate those larger drones into a national airspace. The concept of choice for this problem is the minimum risk configuration (MRC). This means that, instead of maximizing aircraft reliability by including more and more complex system components, the vehicles are routed along dedicated trajectories, so that an eventually occurring accident results in no fatalities and is foreseen to cause only monetary losses. The advantage of the MRC is that the concept can be realized using existing technology, with only moderate effort in new onboard sensory equipment. However, this poses some further challenges concerning air traffic procedures. In Germany and more generally in Europe, the airspace is densely populated, especially in the vicinity of airports. An MRC is meant to interfere with this existing structure in the least possible way. Therefore, an integration concept needs to make sure that the future air cargo system can avoid every potential risk strategically or at least tactically, be it a populated area, industrial infrastructure or other aircraft. We present an integration concept including recommendations for airspace structure, communication infrastructure and information management. Based on publicly available data for population and ground infrastructure, we show exemplary calculations that make the applicability of this concept plausible.

name: Capacity Estimation for Low Altitude Airspace
Strategic Conflict Detection Method for Multi-UAVs in Structured Low-Altitude Airspace
abstract: With the rapid development of UAV technology, ensuring the safe operation of UAVs in structured airspace has become a key issue in urban air traffic management. The paper proposes a strategic framework to determine the potential conflicts in multi-UAV systems by a double-layer detection method. In the first layer of the framework, potential conflict grids are identified by setting both temporal and spatial thresholds in the pre-designed air route network. In the second layer, a local encountering model is established with 3D collision probability estimation to evaluate the severity of conflicts based on the motion information of the UAVs in the air route network, such as position and speed vector. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can determine the potential conflicts of flight schedules efficiently, which also shows the improvement in the precision and reliability of low-altitude air transportation systems.

name: Machine Learning Model Design for Two-Dimensional Photonic Crystals with Point Defects
abstract: The discovery of photonic crystals has opened up a brand-new path for controlling the propagation of light and electromagnetic waves. Its unique photonic bandgap characteristics enable photonic crystals to effectively restrict and regulate the behavior of photons, similar to the bandgap effect of electrons in semiconductors. This study constructs Back Propagation (BP) neural networks, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, leveraging their nonlinear mapping capabilities to accurately predict the bandgap structure and defect mode frequencies of point-defect two-dimensional photonic crystals, significantly enhancing design efficiency. In photonic crystals, by adjusting the parameters of the dielectric column, the band gap structure, band gap position, defect mode, and the intrinsic field distribution of the defect mode can be adjusted. The plane wave propagation method (PWE) and the finite-difference time-domain method (FDTD), which have developed in recent years, as effective numerical calculation methods, have been widely applied in the design and analysis of optical waveguide devices. However, both of these calculation methods require a very large amount of computation, usually necessitating traversal calculations of design parameters, and the calculation time depends on the size, structure, and precision of the device. This study employs BP neural networks, CNN, and LSTM models to predict and optimize structural parameters of point-defect two-dimensional photonic crystals, comparing the performance of different neural network architectures in capturing nonlinear relationships of bandgaps and defect modes, in order to achieve accurate prediction and optimization design of relevant parameters of two-dimensional photonic crystals with point defects.

name: A dynamic airspace planning framework with ADS-B tracks for manned and unmanned aircraft at low-altitude sharing airspace
abstract: Recently civil unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) feature a higher flight altitude and faster cruising speed as UAV market expanding. It causes a potential collision risk to the approaching commercial airliner and general aviation flight at sharing and controlled low-altitude airspace. As a core surveillance technical approved by ICAO, automatic dependent surveillance-broadcast (ADS-B) is realized as an effective method to achieve the monitor of all controlled manned and unmanned aircraft at low-altitude airspace. In this work, a dynamic airspace planning framework based on ADS-B tracks for manned and unmanned aircraft is built. Firstly, an improved Voronoi diagram algorithm is proposed to divide the low-altitude sharing airspace to multiple sectors based on the different assignments of UAVs. Taking advantages of the real-time ADS-B trajectories of manned and unmanned aircraft, a collision risk model between UAVs and manned aircraft is built. Then the initial planned sectors are modified when the potential conflicts between UAVs and manned aircraft are detected. Finally, a revised unmanned aircraft track is planned to reduce the collision probability and send to UAVs' operators. A case study result show the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The built framework can ensure lower safety risk when UAVs and manned aircraft share the low-altitude airspace.

name: A Multi-Candidate Semantic Safe-Corridor Planner for Incremental UAV Path Recovery in Grid-Coded Low-Altitude Airspace
abstract: Semantic updates in grid-coded low-altitude airspace require front-end unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) planners that keep recovery decisions tied to airspace-database records. This paper proposes the Multi-Candidate Semantic Safe-Corridor (MC-SSC) planner as a database-indexed corridor-state and connector-verification layer for incremental path recovery. MC-SSC plans over database level-7 (L7) voxels, activates level-8 (L8) child voxels for corridor-local validation, and maintains a ranked pool of corridor candidates with voxel identifiers, hard-semantic admissibility, update exposure, standby availability, and diagnostic labels. Experiments on database-derived urban airspace windows show that the retained corridor state provides usable standby alternatives, supports faster verified recovery in standby-required and repeated-update settings than global replanning or corridor-reconstruction baselines, and preserves corridor membership during refinement through local L8 validation. The method incurs additional static pool-construction and local-validation cost, and deployed end-to-end reaction time remains outside the measured loop. MC-SSC serves as a tactical database-indexed corridor-decision layer for downstream trajectory optimization and supervisory fail-safe policies.
tags: electrical engineering, electronic engineering, information engineering

name: Behavior Patterns of Chinese Second Language Learners Based on Big Data Analysis
abstract: With the integration of the global economy and the booming development of data technology, Chinese, with its huge user group, is rapidly expanding its international influence, attracting many foreigners to choose to learn as a second language. The rapid development of information networks and artificial intelligence (AI) technology has brought unprecedented opportunities for transformation in the field of education. The application of cutting-edge technologies such as big data and cloud computing has injected strong impetus into the innovation of education models. Given this background, using big data analysis technology to explore the deep connection between students' learning behavior and academic performance has become a key strategy to address the lack of higher-order cognitive ability assessment in the current education evaluation system. This article innovatively proposes a Chinese second language learner academic performance prediction model based on a big data analysis framework, which deeply integrates deep learning (DL) algorithms and can analyze learners' behavioral characteristics in detail. After experimental verification, the model has demonstrated excellent predictive performance, which can help teachers quickly and accurately grasp students' learning progress, and also provide solid data support for developing personalized teaching strategies.

name: FPGA-Based Implementation of DWT and Adaptive Filtering for EMG Signal Processing
abstract: Adaptive filtering and Discrete Wavelet Decomposition are widely regarded as two dominant denoising methods for electromyography (EMG). DWT decomposes original signals into high-frequency and low frequency bands, allowing noise components to be suppressed through thresholding before reconstruction to obtain a cleaner signal However, due to its limited frequency resolution, DWT is not suitable for eliminating narrowband noise such as powerline interference. In contrast, adaptive filtering performs well in removing smallrange frequency since its strong correlation between reference signals and the output. The paper combines two methods and constructs a hybrid denoising system based on FPGA to gain more comprehensive denoising. By comparing two different combinations and considering the performance on FPGA, the result demonstrates that the new system effectively suppresses both broadband white noise and narrowband 50 Hz powerline interference. This hybrid approach highlights a promising direction for non-stationary biomedical signal processing and supports the development of the integration of wearable medical devices.

name: Analysis of Low-Altitude Airspace
abstract: Abstract Low-altitude airspace resources have been the bottleneck of the development of general aviation industry and one of the key factors restricting the development of general aviation in China. Through theoretical research and on-the-spot investigation, this paper constructs a low-altitude airspace resource availability evaluation index system, uses multiple linear regression method to carry out systematic analysis, and determines the index weights at all levels. Taking Jiangsu Province as an example, the present situation of low-altitude available resources in Jiangsu Province is deeply analyzed, the actual situation and a large amount of data in various regions are summarized, the influence values of various factors on the region are calculated, and finally the availability results of low-altitude airspace resources are obtained. The research results demonstrate the scientificity and effectiveness of the method, which can provide reference for the rational utilization of low-altitude airspace resources and the declaration of general aviation activity airspace in China.

name: Difficulty Assessment System of Chinese Vocabulary Acquisition Based on Artificial Intelligence
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, the traditional evaluation method of vocabulary acquisition difficulty, which relies on teachers' experience and intuition, has gradually failed to meet the needs of modern education. By integrating in-depth learning and natural language processing technology, the system realizes multi-dimensional comprehensive evaluation of Chinese vocabulary complexity, frequency of use and language environment. The system consists of five modules: user interface, vocabulary database management, intelligent assessment, personalized learning recommendation and learning progress tracking and feedback, which can provide customized learning suggestions and real-time feedback according to the individual differences of learners. Through the test of 100 different levels of Chinese learners, the results show that the accuracy of the system evaluation is more than 85%, and the user satisfaction is as high as 90%, which significantly improves the learning efficiency and motivation.

name: Safe and Economical UAV Trajectory Planning in Low-Altitude Airspace: A Hybrid DRL-LLM Algorithm With Compliance Awareness_supp1-3668209.pdf
Digital Transformation of University Political Education Courses Using Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning
abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) into university political education addresses key challenges, including low student engagement, limited adaptability to diverse learning needs, and reliance on traditional teaching methods. This study presents a predictive analytics framework designed to optimize political education by leveraging clustering algorithms, decision trees, and neural networks to process and analyze educational data. By utilizing data from Learning Management Systems (LMS), discussion forums, and digital learning tools, the framework enables personalized interventions and adaptive learning experiences. Experimental results reveal that AI-driven approaches significantly enhance learning outcomes, with forum participation rates increasing by 35% and quiz completion rates improving by 27% compared to traditional methods. Additionally, early warning systems built on predictive analytics identified at-risk students with high precision, facilitating timely interventions and achieving an 18% improvement in retention rates. These findings demonstrate the transformative potential of predictive analytics in fostering engagement, improving retention, and enabling dynamic adjustments to course content. By bridging computational technologies and pedagogy, this study establishes a robust and scalable framework for the digital transformation of political education, offering new possibilities to create inclusive and effective learning environments.

name: Virtual Interactive Visualization Modeling Method for ACL Injury Rehabilitation Process Driven by MR
abstract: With the rapid development of hybrid display technology (MR), the field of sports injury rehabilitation has also ushered in new development opportunities. Among them, anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury is one of the most common and difficult types of injuries, while the traditional injury rehabilitation process often has problems such as insufficient individualized rehabilitation and low patient participation. This paper proposes a virtual interactive visualization modeling method for the rehabilitation process of ACL injuries based on MR Technology. By integrating MR, motion acquisition and physiological signal monitoring, an interactive design and realtime response are carried out for the virtual rehabilitation environment. This method can provide patients with an immersive rehabilitation experience and assist doctors in accurately adjusting treatment plans, thereby enhancing treatment efficacy and work efficiency.

name: Scene-Risk-Aware Early Warning of Malicious UAV Intent in Low-Altitude Airspace
abstract: The rapid growth of low-altitude drone operations has created an urgent need for timely and trustworthy security sensing around sensitive facilities. In practical protection scenarios, it is insufficient to classify a target as dangerous only after it has entered a protected region; the system should provide an earlier warning together with interpretable evidence. This paper proposes a scene-risk-aware explainable early-warning framework for malicious drone intent recognition from smoothed low-altitude trajectories. We first develop a security-oriented simulator to generate realistic, curved trajectories for four representative intents, namely normal cruise, accidental intrusion, reconnaissance loiter, and direct attack. The simulator explicitly models a protected core, an alert zone, nominal low-altitude corridors, and scene-risk semantics, and employs spline-based path generation to eliminate unrealistic sharp turns. A dual-branch Transformer is then designed to jointly encode trajectory kinematics and scene-risk features for intent recognition, binary risk estimation, future trajectory prediction, and concept prediction. Instead of outputting only a risk score, the framework provides concept-level evidence, such as a continued approach toward the alert zone, loitering around the protected zone, deviation from the nominal corridor, and range closure toward the core. On 4,800 simulated trajectories, the proposed model achieves 99.72% intent accuracy, a macro-averaged F1 score of 99.73%, an area under the risk-detection curve of 1.000, a concept-prediction micro-averaged F1 score of 0.9554, an average displacement error of 0.0926, and a final displacement error of 0.1508. More importantly, under a strict early-warning evaluation, it achieves a 99.09% detection rate with a mean lead of 11.24 steps at a 3.47% false alarm rate, whereas a standard Transformer baseline achieves only a 74.41% detection rate with a mean lead of 7.18 steps at a 7.51% false alarm rate at the corresponding operating point. These results show that explicit scene-risk modeling is more beneficial for low-altitude warning than trajectory-only sequence modeling optimized mainly for final recognition.

name: Machine Learning-Based Mixed-Flow Production Sequencing Demand Forecasting for H Semiconductor Company
abstract: This paper proposes a demand forecasting model based on machine learning for the mixed-flow production of$\mathbf{H}$Semiconductor company. By constructing the LSTM-XGBoost hybrid model and combining the genetic algorithm to optimize the parameters, the dynamic sorting under multi-dimensional data fusion is realized. Experiments show that the proposed model is significantly superior to traditional methods in terms of prediction accuracy, sorting stability and computational efficiency. The research of this paper provides a reproducible intelligent decisionmaking framework for the semiconductor industry's mixed-flow production.

name: Throughput Efficiency Analysis in Manned-Unmanned Aircraft Integrated Airspace Operations
abstract: With the rapid development of unmanned aircraft technology and the growth of low-altitude economic activities, the trend of large fixed-wing unmanned aircraft entering controlled airspace is becoming increasingly significant, and the demand for their operation is growing more urgent. This paper first analyzes the potential impacts of large unmanned aircraft entering controlled airspace and constructs typical operational scenarios under two modes: segregated airspace operation and integrated airspace operation. Based on this, key variables for manned and unmanned aircraft in airspace operation scenarios are defined, and simulation experiments on airspace operation are conducted under different unmanned aircraft proportion ratios and manned-unmanned switch rates. Through in-depth analysis of the simulation results, this paper explores the impact of segregated and integrated operation modes on airspace utilization and proposes relevant conclusions.

name: Research on the Influence of Rotor Spacing on Lift in Coaxial Dual-Rotor Drones
abstract: Coaxial dual-rotor drones have broad application prospects in both civil and military fields due to their compact structure, strong maneuverability, and portability. However, the aerodynamic interference between the upper and lower rotors of coaxial dual-rotors can significantly affect their aerodynamic performance and lift efficiency. As a key design parameter for regulating the aerodynamic interference of dual rotors, the optimization of rotor spacing is of great importance for improving overall performance. This paper establishes an improved partitioned inflow model based on the blade element momentum theory, taking into account the rotor spacing parameter, and systematically analyzes the influence of different rotor spacings on the lift characteristics and efficiency of coaxial dual-rotors in a hovering state. Using the blade element momentum theory, the disturbed flow field of the lower rotor is divided into two independent uniform flow fields to determine the optimal rotor spacing. Under the experimental conditions of this study, it is found that when the ratio of rotor spacing to rotor radius is between 0.775 and 1, the dual-rotor system operates with high efficiency. In addition, it was observed that when the ratio exceeds 0.55, the rate of increase in total thrust diminishes significantly, and the rate of increase in figure of merit also diminishes significantly.

name: Evaluation Method for Urban Low Altitude Airspace Capacity Based on Hierarchical Topological Airspace
Multi-Objective Path Planning and Energy Efficiency Optimization Method for Industrial Robot Cooperative System
abstract: Aiming at the collaborative optimization problems of efficiency, safety and energy consumption faced by industrial robot collaborative systems in complex scenarios, this study proposes a multi-objective path planning and energy efficiency optimization method. A multi-objective path planning model is constructed, and the improved NSGA-II algorithm is used to solve the Pareto optimal solution with the goal of task completion time, path safety and collision avoidance. A hierarchical energy efficiency optimization model is designed, in which the motion parameters are collected in real time through the energy consumption monitoring layer, the trajectory is adjusted by the dynamic energy consumption function in the path optimization layer, and the balance between energy efficiency and efficiency is realized by the multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm in the decision control layer. The experimental results show that the success rate of path planning is increased from 76.5% to 94.5%, the system energy consumption is reduced by 18.9%, the production efficiency is increased by 21.6%, the operating cost is reduced by 15.3%, and the return on investment cycle is shortened by 37.2%. The research effectively solves the multi-objective collaborative optimization problem of industrial robot collaboration system, which provides theoretical basis and technical support for the green and efficient development of intelligent manufacturing.

name: Router Buffer and Membrane Potential Memory Sharing Mechanism for Spiking Neural Network Hardware Systems
abstract: In traditional spiking neural network (SNN) hardware systems, the use of independent membrane potential memory in neural computing units imposes significant hardware overhead on the system. To address this issue, this paper attempts to store membrane potential information in the internal buffers of routers, thereby realizing the multiplexing of router buffers and membrane potential memory. Compared with traditional SNN hardware systems, this paper avoids the use of independent membrane potential memory inside neural computing units through the optimization of the router architecture, thus reducing the hardware overhead of the entire system.

name: Optimizing Convolutional Neural Network-Based Emotion Recognition: Effects of Layers, Batch Size, and Optimizers
abstract: This paper focuses on the task of emotion recognition. Through experiments on CNN models with different numbers of convolutional layers, performance evaluations are conducted on the selected models under different batch sizes and optimizer Settings. The research background lies in the fact that emotion recognition has significant application value in multiple fields, In practical use for related tasks, current models don't perform flawlessly — there's an opportunity to refine their performance and make them more reliable. During the model construction stage, CNN models with 2-layer, 4-layer, 6-layer, 8-layer, and 10-layer convolutions were designed. First, 40epochs were conducted. Through experimental comparison, it was found that the 8-layer convolutional model performed the best in terms of precision, recall, F1 score, and accuracy, with an accuracy rate of 0.6715. Based on this, the epochs of the experiment was changed to 100, and different batch sizes (8, 16, 32, 64) were tested for the 8-layer model. The results showed that when the batch was 32, the model performed substantively, with an accuracy rate of 0.69 and an accuracy rate of 0.6829. Finally, by comparing the three optimizers Adam, SGD, and Adagrad, the Adam optimizer achieved a model accuracy rate of 0.69 and an accuracy rate of 0.6829, significantly outperforming the other two. In conclusion, this paper clearly states that the 8-layer convolutional CNN model, in combination with the batch 32 and Adam optimizer, performs the best in emotion recognition tasks, providing an effective reference for subsequent research. In the future, model compression technology can be further explored to enhance the feasibility of model deployment in actual scenarios.

name: A Throughput Based Capacity Metric for Low-Altitude Airspace
A Method for Visual Communication Image Style Recognition and Creative Reconstruction Based on Deep Learning
abstract: This study designs a method for visual communication image style recognition and creative reconstruction based on deep learning, aiming to enhance the accuracy of image style recognition and the innovation ability of reconstruction. For image features, a convolutional neural network (CNN) is selected for style recognition. Through style encoding and decoding, as well as depth feature matching, the image style is accurately discriminated and analyzed. At the same time, by means of pixel super-resolution, self-attention generation methods and image texture synthesis, etc., the creative reconstruction of images is achieved. The research results show that the proposed method has achieved good effects in both style discrimination and image creative reconstruction, and can be applied to practical work, demonstrating innovation.

name: Dynamic Credit Scoring Model Enhanced by Machine Learning Algorithms: A Case Study of Sesame Credit
Design of an Attribute Inference Attack Mitigation Algorithm for Sentiment Analysis Tasks in Federated Learning
3D path planning for small UAS operating in low-altitude airspace
abstract: A two step path planning algorithm with collision detection logic for small UAS is proposed. The path planning approach taken in this work is carried out in two steps. In the first step, an initial suboptimal path is generated using A* search. In the second step, a chain of unit masses connected by springs and dampers evolves in a simulated force field, using the A* solution as an initial condition. The chain is described by a set of ordinary differential equations that is driven by virtual forces to find the steady-state equilibrium. A unique strength of this approach is the ability to use dynamic chain analogy to smooth path into a fiyable shape while mainlining a safe distance from intruders. The simulation results show that the proposed approach produces collision-free plans while minimizing the path length.

name: Airworthiness Management of Light Sport Aircraft (LSA) In the Situation of Opening Low-Altitude Airspace
abstract: General aviation industry plays a decisive role in the national economy, “Gradually open up the low-altitude airspace” policy has in fact started providing space for the growth of general aviation, especially for the need of Light Sport Aircraft (LSA). This paper Summary LSA management experience of the United States, through the analysis of management situation of China, gave the LSA operation airworthiness management proposals in the situation of opening low-altitude airspace.

name: Construction of a Basic Nursing Practical Training Operation Action Evaluation Model Based on Deep Learning
abstract: As society's demand for students' basic nursing practical abilities becomes increasingly urgent, the previous reliance solely on manual evaluation models has problems such as subjectivity and heavy workload. This research centers on deep learning technology, applying convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long Short-Term memory networks (LSTM) to accurately judge the operation actions of basic nursing training, collect and label the relevant video activity data of nursing, clean and process the data, and establish a diversified deep learning model, which can identify and evaluate students' nursing skills. The verified results show that This model has high evaluation efficiency and strong accuracy, providing an intelligent teaching assistant for nursing practical training operations.

name: Synthesis and Performance Prediction of Electrode Materials for Sodium Ion Batteries Optimized by Machine Learning
abstract: In order to solve the problem of long development cycle and high cost of sodia-ion battery electrode materials, this study constructed an optimization system based on machine learning to accelerate material discovery and performance prediction. Based on the theory of materials genomics, a hybrid prediction model integrating feature engineering and deep learning is developed, and the synthesis process parameters are optimized by combining reinforcement learning algorithm, and a closed-loop feedback mechanism of design-synthesis-test-optimization is established. Experimental results show that the prediction accuracy of the model for the electrochemical properties of electrode materials is more than 95%, and the research and development cycle is shortened from the traditional 5-8 years to 1-2 years, and the efficiency is improved by 75%. Three to five high-performance candidate materials were successfully screened out from layered oxide, polyanion compound and Prussian blue, and their cycle stability reached more than 1000 times. Studies have confirmed that machine learning technology can significantly reduce research and development costs and time through accurate prediction and process optimization, provide key technical support for the commercial application of sodium ion batteries, and is of great value for promoting energy transition and the realization of the “double carbon” goal.

name: Cotton Futures Forecast Based on LD-BiLSTM
abstract: Traditional statistical and econometric time series forecasting models often show the limitations of modeling ability when dealing with the highly nonlinear, non-stationary and strong noise interference in financial markets. In recent years, deep learning methods, especially long-term and short-term memory networks (LSTM), have been widely used in the field of financial price forecasting because of their advantages in capturing the long-term dependence of time series. However, the complex periodic and trend components in the original price series may interfere with the effective learning of the model and affect the prediction accuracy. Aiming at the above challenges, this paper puts forward a hybrid forecasting model based on learning decompositionforecasting framework (LD-BiLSTM) to improve the forecasting accuracy of cotton futures (CF) price in Zhengzhou Commodity Exchange (ZCE). Based on the 60-minute high-frequency data from 2008 to 2019, the daily data of multiple trading periods are integrated into a daily observation value containing key information such as opening price, highest price, lowest price, closing price (OHLC) and so on. Then, the original daily series is decomposed into two independent components: seasonality and trend by multi-scale decomposition technology. In model design, the seasonal component is input into the deep Bilstm [1] [2] network to capture complex periodic fluctuations, while the trend component extracts long-term evolution characteristics through the full connection layer, and finally fuses the outputs of the two paths to generate prediction results. The empirical results show that the hybrid decompositionforecasting framework can effectively separate and model different dynamic components in the price series, and significantly improve the forecasting accuracy of financial time series.

name: Probabilistic Bird Trajectory Forecasting with Heavy-Tailed Uncertainty Modeling for Low-Altitude Airspace Monitoring
abstract: The low-altitude airspace of bird flocks is gradually shared by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), posing safety risks that necessitate accurate trajectory forecasting. However, existing vision-based methods often treat trajectory prediction and UAV detection as separate tasks, assume light-tailed Gaussian noise, and rely on heavy backbones. These limitations, when applied to bird trajectory forecasting, limit uncertainty calibration and embedded deployment in ground-based monocular surveillance. In this work, we propose a unified framework for low-altitude monitoring. Its core, Mini-BirdFormer, combines a lightweight Transformer encoder with a Student-t mixture density head to model heavy-tailed flight dynamics and produce calibrated uncertainty. Experiments on a real-world dataset show the model achieves strong long-horizon performance with only 1.05 million parameters, attaining a minADE of 0.785 m and reducing negative log-likelihood from 1.25 to −2.01 (lower is better) compared with a Gaussian Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) baseline. Crucially, it enables low-latency inference on resource-constrained platforms at 616 FPS. Additionally, a system-level extension supports zero-shot UAV detection via open-vocabulary learning, attaining 92% recall without false alarms. Results demonstrate that combining heavy-tailed probabilistic modeling with a compact backbone provides a practical, deployable approach for monitoring shared airspace.
tags: electrical engineering, electronic engineering, information engineering

name: Research on the Application of Reinforcement Learning Algorithms in Multi-Objective Scheduling of Construction Engineering
abstract: This paper mainly studies the role of reinforcement learning algorithms in multi-objective scheduling of construction projects. By using the scheduling model of reinforcement learning algorithms, it aims to solve multi-objective problems such as construction period, cost, quality and safety in construction projects. Through techniques such as state discretization, action constraints, and reward function design, reinforcement learning algorithms can adapt to many factors such as the complexity and constraints of engineering scheduling in multi-objective scheduling. Experimental data show that reinforcement learning algorithms have strong flexibility in optimizing task scheduling, resource allocation, cost control, and safety management, etc. It also provides a reference idea for the application research of reinforcement learning algorithms in construction engineering.

name: The primary exploration of alarm chart visualization matching technology in low altitude airspace
abstract: By building an alarm chart platform and the visualization matching model, the design frame of warning chart visualization system in low altitude airspace was explored. Aimed at the types of low altitude flight area and mission requirements, the suitable high resolution remote sensing datum were selected as the data source to establish multi-source remote sensing data collection system. After the extraction of low altitude airspace obstacle data information by classification of geographical obstructions and artificial obstacles, the alarm data information database was established, and low altitude airspace alarm chart plotting platform was constructed. Using airborne GPS system to record aircraft attitude information in real time and to indicate information visualization and combining with special low altitude airspace and obstacle chart database, a chart visualization system and early warning of aircraft can be formed. The results show that preliminary construction of low altitude airspace chart visual matching system framework can provide reference and ideas for future low altitude visual matching system design.

name: A Review of Airspace Designs and Operations for Uas Traffic Management at Low Altitude
Research on Intelligent Integration and Transformation of University Human Resource Systems Driven by New Quality Productivity
